summary: Independent re-verification of TASK-085 (F4 bulk read). Both mandated mutations of apply_read_bulk were re-run and each produced 1 passed / 3 failed, exit 101; the file was restored byte-identically from a backup (sha256 aa04554907e175db3b71e4bbe34787acd50631b435e0c3e327d02c6ed277047e, matching the packet) and 4 passed / 0 failed was re-confirmed after forcing a rebuild. The rewritten (f)/(L1) frontend assertions are strictly stronger than HEAD's. DEC-t084-replace-per-item-ipc-assertions-20260921 exists, accepted, issuer owner, scoped REQ-104/TASK-084, and is referenced in test_review.decision_ids. The doc comments no longer overstate atomicity. Gates recomputed: cargo 206/0/9, lint 0/0, build exit 0, frontend 314/314 (re-run independently).

review_checks.analysis: All six acceptance items hold. set_read_bulk is registered in lib.rs and the bulk path routes through apply_read_bulk -> record_read_state (verified: record_read_state = db::set_read + db::enqueue_sync with read/unread), so per-id is_read writes and sync_queue enqueue match the per-item path. reader.ts markEntriesReadBulk now issues a single api.setReadBulk call, and (f)/(L1) assert exactly one set_read_bulk with zero set_read. (L1) pins the exact id set 101,103,104,105,201,301. The replaced assertions are authorised by an owner decision, and no file outside the five allowed paths changed.

The equivalence test now calls the real apply_read_bulk rather than a copy-pasted loop. I re-ran both mutations independently: bypassing record_read_state via crate::db::set_read, and skipping enqueue for the first id only, each gave 1 passed / 3 failed at exit 101, so the evidence is load-bearing rather than decorative. The rewritten (f)/(L1) replacements are at least as strict as HEAD: (L1) was upgraded from a payload-length check to the exact sorted id set plus exactly-one-set_read_bulk and zero-set_read, and (f) keeps its exact 101,103 id-set check.

apply_read_bulk_empty_is_noop locks the empty-ids no-write/no-enqueue path, and the command short-circuits empty ids before taking the lock. apply_read_bulk_false_queues_unread_actions locks read=false to is_read=0 plus the mutually exclusive unread enqueue. A mid-batch error propagates via ? and leaves prior ids committed and enqueued; this partial-commit behaviour is now truthfully documented instead of being claimed atomic, and the frontend catches the rejection into a single toast so no unhandled rejection escapes.

Extracting apply_read_bulk mirrors the existing apply_mark_all_read pattern, keeping command and test on one real code path and removing the duplicated-loop hazard that produced the original decorative evidence. The new test module is small and self-contained with focused helpers (seeded/count_read/queued). Naming and the read/unread action strings are unchanged, and no new dependency or module boundary was introduced.

This is a static improvement with no benchmark claimed, which matches the evidence available: the change converts N invoke round-trips into one and holds the DB lock once with a single schedule_state_push instead of one per id. No measured throughput figure is asserted anywhere in the diff, so no unmeasured performance claim is being made. Per-id record_read_state still commits individually, so the win is IPC and lock amortisation rather than write batching.
